case_name: Tribeca Skin Care v. AccessiBe Ltd.
court: U.S. District Court (jurisdiction details pending confirmation)
docket: Filed June 24, 2024 — docket not confirmed in public sources
claim_type: AccessiBe misrepresented that its overlay widget (AccessWidget) makes websites ADA compliant; Tribeca Skin Care was sued for ADA non-compliance despite having AccessiBe installed and paying $490/year
outcome: Active litigation as of 2024 — Tribeca sued AccessiBe for deceptive marketing; FTC separately fined AccessiBe $1M in April 2025
estimated_defense_cost: Tribeca paid $490/year for AccessiBe and still faced ADA lawsuit; total defense costs from both lawsuits not disclosed

sources.name: Comm Law Group — AccessiBe faces class action lawsuit
Law Office of Lainey Feingold — New class action lawsuit against AccessiBe (July 2024)

summary_one_line: A small dermatology practice paid $490/year for an accessibility widget, got sued for ADA violations anyway, then sued the widget vendor — and the FTC fined the vendor $1M in 2025 for deceptive marketing.
notes: Tribeca Skin Care purchased AccessiBe's AccessWidget in August 2022 for $490/year. In January 2024, Tribeca was sued in an ADA class action despite having the widget installed. Tribeca then filed suit against AccessiBe. The FTC's $1M fine against AccessiBe (April 2025) independently confirms that overlays do not constitute ADA compliance. Over 800 businesses using AccessiBe were sued in 2023-2024 (UsableNet data). FTC action primary source should be confirmed with FTC press release before publication.
